messages:
incident-bot: PAGER 134 SEV1: multiple NCCL communicator resets and container crashes observed in tp-serving pool (us-west-2). Symptoms: NCCL TIMEOUT, GPU Xid entries, node flaps, surge in 5xx. Affected service: model-infer-prod. Paging oncall. thread:1749056789

maya (oncall): I'm on it. Which nodes first? Any obvious network flaps or recent kernel updates?

gina (ml-infra): Logging snapshot: several runtime workers hit NCCL_TIMEOUT and then exit. Example from worker log on gpu-21-4:```
[2025-09-03T11:12:03Z] NCCL WARN timeout in allGather after 60000 ms
[2025-09-03T11:12:03Z] ncclCommInitRank failed: Unhandled system error
[2025-09-03T11:12:04Z] runtime: process crashed (SIGSEGV)
```
Also host says GPU 0 Xid 43 (PCIe link error) and one NVLINK error. nvidia-smi shows Pending Reset on GPU 0.

frank (infra): Current node list with recent GPU errors: gpu-21-4, gpu-22-2, gpu-22-6. No scheduled kernel patches this morning, but we did push a microcode/kernel backport earlier in the rack last week. I'll run health checks on the IB fabric and PCIe errors.

harry (sre): Customer impact: 3.1% 5xx in last 10m. Top impacted tenants: EchoAnalytics and BetaLabs. We should enable routing fallback and reduce per-pod capacity temporarily to avoid cascades.

maya (oncall): Action plan: 1) quick env tweak to make NCCL fail fast and avoid stuck collectives (set NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1, NCCL_TIMEOUT=30000); 2) adjust routing: route 30% to single-gpu fallback variant for us-west-2; 3) cordon+drain a canary node (gpu-21-4) and restart driver/kernel modules; 4) if stable, roll. Doing 1 now.

gina (ml-infra): Pushing DS env patch to model-router in serving ns:```bash
kubectl -n serving set env ds/model-router NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_TIMEOUT=30000 --record
```
deploy-bot: deploy started for ds/model-router @ 1749056845 by gina (ml-infra)

maya (oncall): Routing tweak in progress: routing-service updated -> fallback 30% for us-west-2 for 15m.

iris (support): Notifying customers: initial status posted to status.redwood.ai. Flagging EchoAnalytics and BetaLabs for priority updates.

frank (infra): Beginning canary on gpu-21-4. Steps: cordon -> drain -> check for stale processes -> restart nvidia driver -> check dmesg for PCIe errors -> uncordon. Executing now.

gina (ml-infra): Observing fewer stuck collectives after env patch, but I still see some communicator init failures during pod start:```
[2025-09-03T11:15:22Z] ncclCommInitRank failed: NCCL_UNSUPPORTED_ERROR
[2025-09-03T11:15:23Z] worker failed to allocate KV cache: CUDA out of memory
```
Suggest we also reduce model prefetch and limit max_sequence temporarily. I'll apply a conservative config override for new pods.

frank (infra): Canary driver restart done on gpu-21-4. dmesg shows a burst of PCIe AER errors at the time of crash, then GPU reset. Cleared UVM and reloaded driver. Pods rescheduled. Observed one pod OOM during restart; I manually killed leftover cuda processes.

harry (sre): Keep an eye on error rate. If OOMs spike we should throttle concurrency on freshly scheduled pods. Delta now: 5xx down to 1.0% from 3.1% after routing + env patch.

gina (ml-infra): Change applied: reduce KV cache to 25% and set MAX_SEQ=2048 for canary pods. Rolling these limits to the autoscaler config for 10m window.

maya (oncall): Plan to roll kernel/driver refresh across gpu-22 nodes next, one at a time with 5m gap. frank, coordinate. Keep fallback routing until last node done.

frank (infra): Starting roll on gpu-22-2. Noting a node with repeated NVLINK errors; I'm opening a hardware ticket if it persists. Roll script:```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-22-2
kubectl drain gpu-22-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
ssh gpu-22-2 sudo systemctl stop nvidia-docker && sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia_drv && sudo modprobe nvidia_drv nvidia_uvm
# check dmesg, nv-hostengine logs
sudo systemctl start nvidia-docker
kubectl uncordon gpu-22-2
```

frank (infra): Update: during restart on gpu-22-2, one GPU failed to come back cleanly (persistent reset). I flagged that node for reimage; shifting pods away.

gina (ml-infra): We are throttling concurrency for rescheduled pods and setting a per-pod env var to skip heavy prefetch for 5m. This reduced OOMs during reschedules.

harry (sre): Monitoring: error rate steady ~0.8%. Latency p50 unchanged, p99 slightly elevated due to some fallback routing. Support notifications sent.

maya (oncall): Handing over long-running rollout to night team at 1749057000. Summary: env changes applied (NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1, NCCL_TIMEOUT=30000), routing fallback 30%, driver roll initiated on affected nodes, per-pod memory caps applied. Handoff notes in incident ticket.

iris (support): Posting follow-up with timeline and customer impact estimates. Will arrange post-incident call for EchoAnalytics + BetaLabs if requested.

gina (ml-infra): Follow-ups: collect nv-hostengine logs, IB counters, and NCCL debug traces (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) from the impacted job runs. We'll correlate with firmware/kernel versions. Opening postmortem doc.

deploy-bot: auto-rollback rule armed for ds/model-router if 5xx > 1.5% for 5m.

maya (oncall): Leaving the channel. Re-pager if error rate creeps back above 1.5%. Thanks team.

harry (sre): Taking over for rollout and HW triage. I'll keep updates in-thread and on the bridge.

incident-bot: Incident ticket #INC-20250903-087 opened. Severity: 1. Please attach kernel/driver versions and NCCL logs to the ticket for RCA.

notes: short timeline: 11:12 initial alert -> 11:14 env patch -> 11:16 routing adjusted -> 11:17 canary driver restart -> 11:23 first roll node -> 11:30 handoff to night oncall.
